explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full microsoft-privacy system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The evaluation covered the primary user flows across the four main pages of the privacy dashboard clone, identifying critical layout and functional barriers. While complex flows like data download requests and bulk deletion modals work well, several local interactions—such as the browse history time filter, individual item deletion, and the 'Discard changes' button in ad settings—are unresponsive. Furthermore, mobile usability is significantly degraded by page-level horizontal overflow and persistently small touch targets. Note that only 41% of interactive features were explicitly exercised, meaning many footer links and secondary settings remain untested.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the Microsoft Privacy dashboard clone, focusing on settings toggles, data deletion flows, and the data download form across desktop and mobile viewports.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start on the main privacy dashboard to verify global navigation and activity cards. It will then deep-dive into the Browse History page to test filtering and destructive actions (single/bulk delete). Next, the run will cover Ad Settings to validate complex toggle interactions and interest selection. Finally, it will walk through the multi-step Download Data form and re-test critical interactive flows on a mobile viewport.
assumptions: Settings toggles provide immediate visual feedback (e.g., 'Saving...' or state change) rather than requiring a separate submit button.
'Clear all' in browse history and 'Clear' in the dashboard trigger modal dialogs requiring secondary confirmation.
Form submission on download-data.html provides success feedback but doesn't actually trigger a file download.
risk_hotspots: The 'Clear all' modal dialog in browse-history.html and any corresponding dialog on index.html.
Interaction between the master 'See ads that interest you' toggle and the service-specific toggles in ad-settings.html.
Small tap targets in the global navigation and header, especially on mobile.

phases.title: Dashboard & Navigation
phases.objective: Verify the main dashboard layout, global navigation links, and activity card entry points.
key_checks: Check functionality of global header links and user menu.
Interact with top-level 'Privacy settings' toggles and observe feedback.
Verify that 'Manage browse activity' and 'Download your data' buttons route to correct sub-pages.
exit_criteria: Successfully navigated to browse-history.html, ad-settings.html, and download-data.html from the index.

phases.title: Browse History Management
phases.objective: Validate activity filtering and deletion interactions.
key_checks: Delete a single row using the per-row trash icon and observe animation/removal.
Click 'Clear all' and interact with the resulting modal confirmation.
exit_criteria: Filters manipulated, single row deleted, and 'Clear all' modal successfully confirmed or dismissed.

phases.title: Ad Personalization Settings
phases.objective: Test hierarchical toggle states and multi-select interactions.
key_checks: Toggle the master 'See ads that interest you' switch.
Toggle individual service switches (e.g., Microsoft consumer apps, Bing & Edge) and check dependency on master switch.
Select and deselect various 'Ad topics' checkboxes.
exit_criteria: Master toggle, sub-toggles, and interest checkboxes have been exercised and state changes verified.

phases.title: Data Download Flow
phases.objective: Complete the multi-step form to request a data archive.
key_checks: Select specific data categories (e.g., Account profile, Browse activity) instead of 'Include everything'.
Submit the form and observe success or validation states.

phases.title: Mobile Usability
phases.objective: Verify that complex layouts and dense navigation are usable on small screens.
key_checks: Check how the global navigation bar and 'small tap targets' adapt on mobile.
Verify that the activity card grid collapses properly on index.html.
Ensure data tables and filter bars in browse-history.html are usable without horizontal scrolling.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout assessed for overlap, horizontal scroll, and touch target size.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise settings toggles, modal dialogs, select dropdowns, and form submission.
coverage_targets.mobile: Re-run index navigation and browse history deletion flow on mobile viewport.

notes: Many small tap targets were flagged in the prescan; pay close attention to the top black ribbon and secondary nav usability, especially during the mobile phase.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the browse history page on a mobile device
findings.problem: The page experiences horizontal overflow on mobile viewports, forcing users to pan horizontally to view content and cutting off secondary navigation elements.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings and trajectory notes indicate that the 'Browse history' page width is 495px while the mobile viewport is only 390px. The secondary navigation menu (containing 'Subscriptions', 'Payments & billing') overflows and is partially cut off.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal scrolling on a predominantly vertical mobile interface breaks the mental model and forces awkward gestures, making it difficult for users to discover and access off-screen navigation items.
findings.suggestion: Implement a responsive layout for the secondary navigation, such as a horizontal scrolling container with visual overflow cues or a collapsible hamburger menu for mobile viewports. Ensure structural containers do not exceed 100vw.

findings.user_goal: Interact with links and action buttons on a touch screen
findings.problem: Numerous interactive elements have tap target sizes significantly below the recommended minimum of 44x44px for touch interfaces.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings highlight that top global navigation links (e.g., 'Microsoft', 'Gaming') are 19px tall, the 'Clear all browse history' button is 34px tall, and individual 'Delete entry' trash icons are 26x27px.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets lead to high interaction friction, increased error rates, and frustration for users on mobile devices, especially when destructive actions like delete buttons are positioned close to other elements.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and minimum height/width of clickable elements to ensure they meet the WCAG recommended 44x44px target size on mobile layouts.

findings.user_goal: Filter browse history by a specific time range
findings.problem: The 'Time range' dropdown filter on the browse history page is unresponsive and does not filter the displayed data.
findings.evidence: Trajectory notes from steps 01-06 state that attempting to change the 'Time range' filter (e.g., to 'Last 7 days') neither updates the dropdown's selected value visually nor filters the history table.
findings.why_it_matters: Users looking for specific past activities will be unable to narrow down a potentially massive list of history entries, rendering the data management tool ineffective.
findings.suggestion: Implement the necessary JavaScript event listeners to capture the 'change' event on the `<select>` element and filter the data table accordingly.

findings.user_goal: Discard unwanted changes made to ad personalization settings
findings.problem: The 'Discard changes' button does not revert modified checkboxes or dismiss the active warning message.
findings.evidence: In chunk steps-37-42, clicking the 'Discard changes' button after checking an unselected ad topic failed to revert the visual state of the checkboxes or remove the '⚠ You have unsaved changes.' warning.
findings.why_it_matters: If users make accidental changes to their privacy topics and cannot discard them, they may feel forced to save unwanted settings or abandon the page entirely, damaging trust in the privacy controls.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the 'Discard changes' button is bound to an event handler that resets the form inputs to their initial loaded state and hides the unsaved changes warning banner.

findings.user_goal: Delete a single entry from the browse history
findings.problem: Clicking the trash can icon next to an individual history entry does not delete the item or provide any visual feedback.
findings.evidence: Trajectory notes from steps 01-06 confirm that the per-row delete icon is unresponsive, failing to remove the target entry or trigger a deletion animation.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect immediate visual confirmation when deleting data. A lack of response leaves them uncertain whether the data was actually removed from Microsoft's servers.
findings.suggestion: Attach an event listener to the trash icons that removes the corresponding row from the DOM (perhaps with a brief fade-out animation) and updates the backend state.

findings.user_goal: Navigate and toggle ad settings using a screen reader or keyboard
findings.problem: The main ad personalization toggles are not recognized as standard interactive elements in the DOM accessibility tree.
findings.evidence: Trajectory chunk steps-07-12 indicates that the main ad toggles are visually present but missing from the accessibility tree.
findings.why_it_matters: Users relying on assistive technologies will be entirely unable to perceive, navigate to, or operate the primary privacy toggles, blocking them from managing their ad preferences.
findings.suggestion: Implement the custom toggles using standard `<button>` or `<input type="checkbox">` elements. If custom divs must be used, ensure they possess `role="switch"`, `tabindex="0"`, and correct `aria-checked` states that update dynamically.
